transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 17:43 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Sofia Ramirez (Redwood SE), Mark Davenport (Pinnacle CTO), Lisa Chen (Head of Infrastructure), Rahul Singh (DevOps), Priya Malhotra (Security)

Summary: brief discovery on Private/VPC deployment options for healthcare data workloads. Focus on VPC peering, private endpoints, region constraints, KMS integration, and compliance.

Topics: network topology, peering vs private endpoints, egress controls, region availability, encryption/KMS, SSO/SCIM, pilot timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining uh i'm jordan from redwood inference, i'm the AE on this one, really appreciate you all taking the time. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Mark Davenport: good, thanks jordan. busy week but excited to talk through this.
[00:10] Lisa Chen: yeah hi all, lisa here, we'll mostly talk VPC and networking needs.
[00:14] Rahul Singh: rahul, devops, will ask about peering and routing.
[00:18] Priya Malhotra: priya, security, i'll cover compliance questions.
[00:22] Sofia Ramirez: hi i'm sofia, solutions engineer, i'll drive the technical bits. quick agenda: 1) high-level infra ask 2) network options (peering/private endpoint) 3) auth and KMS 4) next steps. sound good?
[00:32] Mark Davenport: yep good. we are evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private — for pinnacles' patient data workloads we lean private. key asks: no public internet egress for inference, data residency in us-east, and strong audit logs.
[00:46] Jordan Lee: noted. when you say no public egress, do you mean the model traffic itself needs to stay within your VPC and never traverse public endpoints?
[00:54] Mark Davenport: correct. models and inference must be inside our VPC or talk over private link/peering only. we can't have tokens or PHI touching public internet.
[01:03] Sofia Ramirez: understood. we support a Private deployment: control plane can be customer-managed or redwood-managed with private connectivity. typical patterns are VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, or site-to-site VPN for on-prem.
[01:16] Lisa Chen: can you outline differences? peering vs private link — which is recommended for multi-account setups?
[01:23] Sofia Ramirez: sure. VPC peering is direct routing between VPCs, low latency, but doesn't support transitive routing, so you need peering per VPC. PrivateLink (AWS NLB + interface endpoints) gives you controlled private endpoints that scale and are easier across accounts. For our customers who want strict network controls and multi-account, PrivateLink is often preferred.
[01:43] Rahul Singh: okay, what about cross-region? we have services in us-east-1 and us-west-2, want inference close to data to reduce latency. can private link work cross-region?
[01:54] Sofia Ramirez: PrivateLink is regional; you need endpoints per region. We can deploy Redwood Private in each region you need, or set up a routing layer — but for strict residency we'd typically deploy in us-east-1 only. if you need both, we recommend multi-region Private deployments and sync via our control plane.
[02:13] Priya Malhotra: how about encryption - keys must be customer-managed. we use AWS KMS CMKs and want HSM-backed keys.
[02:22] Jordan Lee: yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS via cross-account key policies or bring-your-own KMS in your account. we have docs for KMS key policies and HSM integrations. sofia can share details.
[02:33] Sofia Ramirez: quick caveat — if control plane is redwood-managed, we'll need IAM role setup or cross-account key grants. if control plane is customer-managed entirely inside your VPC, it's simpler: keys stay in your account. we'll share the exact policy snippets.
[02:46] Mark Davenport: okay. audit logs are critical — we need detailed request/response-level logs for compliance. does private mode preserve logs in our S3 buckets?
[02:57] Sofia Ramirez: yes, for Private we can forward audit logs to your S3 or CloudWatch. there's also an option to keep logs on-prem via our connector. retention and access controls are configurable.
[03:10] Lisa Chen: what about egress for model updates and vulnerability patches — do appliances need outbound internet at all?
[03:18] Jordan Lee: generally, node images may need controlled outbound for patching. we support an allowlist pattern where nodes pull from an internal mirror or via a proxy in your network. some customers use a maintenance window with tightly controlled egress via NAT.
[03:31] Rahul Singh: latency is a concern. if we run models in us-east-1 but data is in us-west-2, what's the perf hit? can you share any numbers?
[03:40] Sofia Ramirez: rough guidances: cross-region adds 50-150ms additional latency depending on model size and sequence length; for small LLMs it might be 50-80ms extra, larger models can be higher. we recommend co-locating high-TPS endpoints with data. we can run a benchmark POC to measure exact numbers.
[03:56] Mark Davenport: benchmarks will be important. we need to validate throughput under our payloads, also cost delta between dedicated vs private.
[04:03] Jordan Lee: agreed — we can run a proof-of-concept: pilot in us-east-1 with a 3-node config, run your sample workload, measure p99 latency and token cost. sofia will map out sizing.
[04:14] Sofia Ramirez: noted. Rahul, can you describe your expected QPS and typical sequence lengths?
[04:20] Rahul Singh: roughly 150 QPS peak, 30 QPS steady, sequences around 256 tokens mostly, sometimes spikes to 1024 for full reports.
[04:29] Sofia Ramirez: great, that helps. we'll do a sizing estimate for both dedicated and private. dedicated reserved capacity gives more predictable throughput, private gives more isolation but can cost a bit more to run per node depending on utilization.
[04:42] Priya Malhotra: SSO and SCIM — we use Okta, need role-based access and SAML integration. do you support that?
[04:49] Jordan Lee: yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning both for hosted and private. for Private deployments, you can run the auth provider inside your network and we point the console to that.
[05:01] Lisa Chen: any special network ports or firewall rules we need to open?
[05:06] Sofia Ramirez: we'll send a checklist but high level: control plane to management endpoints (for redwood-managed control plane) over interface endpoints; node-to-node comms uses internal ports (we provide range). for PrivateLink, you need the interface endpoint ENIs in subnets. we can provide minimal port list.
[05:22] Mark Davenport: licensing and pricing — can you give a sense?
[05:25] Jordan Lee: rough tiers: hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits; Private has a platform fee + support, and infra costs are passed through (you can bring your infra). we'll send the pricing sheet.
[05:36] Rahul Singh: question about model variants & fallbacks — if we pin a model version, can Redwood route to a cheaper quantized variant automatically when capacity constrained?
[05:47] Sofia Ramirez: yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible variants by policy — you can set latency vs cost preferences. note: fallback changes can affect output quality — recommend evals.
[05:58] Mark Davenport: on the security front, SOC2/ISO - do you have those certifications?
[06:03] Jordan Lee: yes we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001; for Private deployments we provide the compliance artifacts and we can do an ATO packet. we'll share redacted reports.
[06:13] Priya Malhotra: do you support VPC peering with transit gateway to reduce peering sprawl?
[06:19] Sofia Ramirez: transit gateway is supported for routing but depends on cloud provider constraints. with Transit Gateway you can reduce peering count, but you still need routing rules; some customers prefer PrivateLink for simpler cross-account.
[06:32] Lisa Chen: how does billing work for Private? we want chargeback visibility per team.
[06:37] Jordan Lee: we export usage and cost metrics; you can integrate with your billing pipeline or we can provide per-project usage reports.
[06:45] Rahul Singh: any constraints on AMI/custom images? we sometimes require custom hardened images.
[06:51] Sofia Ramirez: we support custom images for on-prem appliances or customer-managed nodes; redwood-managed nodes use our hardened image but we can work through a security review for custom AMIs.
[07:02] Mark Davenport: timebox for pilot — we'd like a 4-week POC starting mid march, with goals: validate latency, throughput, and compliance artifacts.
[07:12] Jordan Lee: sounds reasonable. target dates: kick off first week of 2026-03-16?
[07:17] Mark Davenport: yes that works.
[07:21] Sofia Ramirez: okay i'll capture requirements: CIDR ranges, regions (you mentioned us-east-1 primary; confirm us-west-2 for a later phase), expected QPS and sample payloads, and compliance checklist from priya.
[07:34] Priya Malhotra: we'll provide data classification and the exact retention policies. also need to know how long logs are retained by default.
[07:42] Sofia Ramirez: default retention is 30 days but configurable; for Private we can set retention to your policy and ship to your S3.
[07:49] Jordan Lee: any blockers we should know now?
[07:52] Lisa Chen: main blockers: legal needs a runbook for ingress/egress, security needs KMS policy examples, and network needs clear port list and peering options. once we have those we can sign off on pilot infra.
[08:05] Jordan Lee: perfect — we'll send the docs.
[08:08] [brief cross-talk about calendar invites and times]
[08:20] Sofia Ramirez: quick note on private endpoints: we can expose inference endpoints as interface endpoints in your VPC, you control the subnets and NACLs, connection never goes through public internet. for model updates we can use in-VPC mirrored registries.
[08:33] Rahul Singh: do you support endpoint policies for specific principals? we want to lock which IAM roles can call endpoints.
[08:38] Sofia Ramirez: yes, endpoint policies and IAM conditions are supported. you can restrict by principal, VPC, or source IP.
[08:46] Mark Davenport: one more thing — regulatory: some of our data must stay in us-east-1 region only. can we ensure our Private deployment is single-region and isolated?
[08:56] Jordan Lee: absolutely, we can configure a single-region Private deployment with control plane and compute in your region only. we'll provide architecture diagrams showing no cross-region traffic.
[09:06] Priya Malhotra: any SLA for Private?
[09:09] Jordan Lee: Private deployments can come with SLA in enterprise plans; we'll include proposed SLA terms in the proposal.
[09:17] Lisa Chen: ok, let's recap next steps.
[09:19] Jordan Lee: recap: we'll send private deployment architecture doc, KMS policy examples, network checklist, pricing sheet, and propose pilot timeline for mid-March. sofia will produce sizing and benchmark plan. rahul will provide CIDR and sample payloads. priya will share compliance list.
[09:34] Mark Davenport: that captures it. thanks everyone.
[09:38] Jordan Lee: thanks all — we'll follow up via email and attach the docs.
[09:42] Sofia Ramirez: i'll set up the follow-up technical deep dive; expect a calendar invite.
[09:46] Meeting end.
